questions.q: How is console markup like '[bold red]hello[/]' turned into styled text, including closing tags?

How does a table decide the width of each column when the content does not fit the available width?
How is a style definition string such as 'bold italic red on white' parsed into a style object?
How does a regex-based highlighter apply styles to the parts of a text that match its patterns?
How does the console look up a named style from the theme, falling back to parsing the name as a style definition?
Where is console output that has been buffered (for example inside a 'with console:' block) actually written to the terminal?
How does a live display refresh itself automatically a given number of times per second in the background?
How is an exception turned into a rich traceback, including its chained causes and the local variables of each frame?
How does track() wrap an iterable so that a progress bar advances as items are consumed?
